subject.title: feat: add codexbar guard — quota-aware exit code to gate automation

question: Should CodexBar own a stable quota-gating command whose defaults and exit statuses become a public automation API?
rationale: Correcting the implementation is mechanical, but selecting the permanent threshold, window fallback, fail-open policy, flag shape, and exit-code contract requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Sponsor the guard contract
options.body: Accept the feature direction, then require parity with existing account and metric-selection behavior plus documented, proven command semantics before merge.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Ship only an explicitly selected window and threshold, omitting defaults or fail-open behavior until their policy is established.

options.title: Keep the CLI reporting-only
options.body: Decline the dedicated gate and leave callers to interpret existing machine-readable usage output.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the guard contract
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction, then require parity with existing account and metric-selection behavior plus documented, proven command semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is the strongest available owner for accepting or rejecting a new public CLI automation contract.
